questions.q: What best describes an Azure Machine Learning workspace?
options: A virtual machine you log in to and run notebooks on
The top-level resource that organizes jobs, data assets, models and endpoints and keeps the history of your runs
A Docker image that contains your training code
A pricing tier that unlocks GPU compute
questions.explain: The workspace is the top-level Azure ML resource: it groups the artifacts of a project, records run history (logs, metrics, script snapshots), and hosts compute and datastore configuration.

questions.q: Which companion resource stores secrets that the workspace and its compute targets need?
options: Azure Container Registry
Application Insights
Azure Key Vault
The default storage account
questions.explain: Key Vault holds secrets. The storage account holds logs and uploads, Application Insights holds endpoint diagnostics, and Container Registry holds Docker images for custom environments.

questions.q: In the SDK v2, what do you create first so that later calls can create compute, submit jobs and register models?
options: An MLClient connected to your subscription, resource group and workspace
A Docker container running scikit-learn
A requirements.txt file
A Key Vault secret named ml_client
questions.explain: MLClient is the handle to a workspace. You can build it from IDs directly or with MLClient.from_config, which reads a config.json downloaded from the studio.

questions.q: Why does Microsoft's guidance suggest creating one workspace per project?
options: Azure limits each subscription to one workspace
Workspaces cannot contain more than one model
It lets cost reporting and configuration such as datastores be scoped to each project
It is required before you can use Microsoft Entra groups
questions.explain: A workspace can serve several projects, but limiting it to one keeps cost reporting and configuration like datastores scoped per project.

questions.q: The lesson's code for creating a workspace is labeled 'not run here'. What does that tell you?
options: The code is invalid and should never be used
It is illustrative: running it needs a real Azure subscription, so the course shows it without executing it
MLClient can only be used inside the studio
The code only works on Linux
questions.explain: The course has no Azure account to execute against, so cloud snippets are drawn from Microsoft Learn and clearly marked as illustrative. Always check the current docs when adapting them.
